questions.question: Profit rose from ₹87.92 crore in FY24 to ₹116.79 crore in FY26, but only 60.6% of operating profit came in as cash. What does that suggest?

choices.text: The business is doing brilliantly; cash doesn't matter.
Some profit may be stuck in unpaid bills or unsold goods, so check how fast customers pay.
The company must have paid a big dividend.
Profit and cash are always equal, so the figures must be wrong.

questions.explanation: Profit is counted when a sale is made; cash arrives when the customer pays. For HD Fire Protect Limited, only 60.6% of operating profit turned into cash, so money is getting stuck. Trade receivables and inventory are where to look.

questions.question: At the top price, HD Fire Protect Limited's P/E is 40.7x. Similar listed companies have a P/E of about 47.5x. What does that tell you?

choices.text: It costs about the same as, or less than, similar companies for each rupee of profit.
It costs more than similar companies for each rupee of profit, so its profit must grow faster to be worth it.
The P/E shows how many shares the company has.

questions.explanation: A P/E of 40.7x against 47.5x means you pay no more for each rupee of HD Fire Protect Limited's profit than for its peers'. That is a fair starting point, not a guarantee.

questions.question: 0.2% of this IPO's money is an offer for sale. Where does that part of the money go?

choices.text: Into the company, to build new factories.
To the existing owners who are selling their shares.

questions.explanation: In an offer for sale, existing owners sell shares they already hold, so the money goes to them. Only the fresh issue, ₹710.56 crore here, reaches HD Fire Protect Limited.

questions.question: Sales went from ₹372.95 crore in FY24 to ₹489.28 crore in FY26, which is 14.5% a year. How would you describe that?
questions.explanation: 14.5% a year is slow growth: HD Fire Protect Limited is growing, but not by much.
